parts.label: Magnitude of total potential energy, greatest first
parts.explanation: The two fixed pair distances are d and D; the third is smallest in 1, equal in 2 and 4, and largest in 3.

reasoning: For the referenced Checkpoint 2 diagrams, third distances are D−d, √(D²+d²), D+d, √(D²+d²). Since |U|=Gm²(1/d+1/D+1/rthird), the ordering follows. Checked the actual checkpoint diagram on chapter page 5.
assumptions: Use the masses, radii, axes and symmetry shown in the source figure.

parts.label: a · Sphere masses, greatest first
parts.explanation: Matching exterior curves GM/r² mean equal total mass.

parts.label: b · Sphere densities, greatest first
parts.explanation: Mean density is proportional to M/R³; equal-mass planets have larger density at smaller radius.

reasoning: Visual graph audit: curves 1 and 2 share the higher exterior curve, while 3 and 4 share the lower one. The graph gives R₁<R₂=R₃<R₄. Since ρ is proportional to M/R³, the equal-mass pairs obey ρ₁>ρ₂ and ρ₃>ρ₄; at equal radius R₂=R₃ the larger mass gives ρ₂>ρ₃. This verifies the full density ranking without inferring any unplotted interior field.
assumptions: Compare mean density M/(4πR³/3); the horizontal axis uses a common fixed radial scale.

parts.label: a · Original force direction
parts.explanation: Equal symmetric horizontal components cancel; both vertical components point upward.

parts.label: b · Direction after C is moved radially away
parts.answer: Tilts toward B, approaching the A-to-B direction
options: Tilts toward B, approaching the A-to-B direction
Tilts toward C, approaching the A-to-C direction
parts.explanation: Moving C away weakens its attraction; B’s unchanged force increasingly dominates.

reasoning: Vector superposition first gives Fx=0,Fy>0. As C’s radius increases, its contribution decreases as 1/rC², so the resultant rotates toward B and reaches that ray only in the limit rC→∞. The limiting rotation is θ counterclockwise from +y, as marked in the diagram. This checks both the initial symmetry and limiting case.
assumptions: Use the masses, radii, axes and symmetry shown in the source figure.

parts.label: a · Potential-energy change for the six paths
parts.answer: The same for all six paths
options: The same for all six paths
Zero only for the straight path
parts.explanation: Gravitational potential energy depends only on the endpoints.

parts.label: b · Work done by gravity for the six paths
parts.answer: The same for all six paths
options: The same for all six paths
Different whenever the paths have different lengths
parts.explanation: Gravity is conservative, so Wg=−ΔU regardless of the route.

reasoning: Every path has common start a and end b. ΔU=GMm(1/ra−1/rb), and Wg=−ΔU. The endpoint formula verifies path independence without assuming a constant gravitational force.
assumptions: Use the masses, radii, axes and symmetry shown in the source figure.

parts.label: Effective free-fall acceleration, greatest first
parts.answer: b = d = f > e > c > a
options: b = d = f > e > c > a
a = c = e > f > d > b
b > d > f > a > c > e
parts.explanation: Poles have no rotational reduction; equatorial acceleration is GM/R²−ω²R, with the fastest rotation giving the smallest value.

reasoning: The diagram labels a,c,e at the equators of the 16 h,24 h,48 h planets and b,d,f at the poles. Equal masses/radii give identical gravitational acceleration. Subtracting (2π/T)²R only at the equators verifies e>c>a and equality of all poles.
assumptions: Equal spherical masses and radii; effective acceleration is measured relative to each rotating surface; ignore oblateness.

parts.label: Work by gravity from infinity, greatest first
parts.explanation: Gravity does positive work equal to minus the final potential energy; the middle location is closest to both source masses.

reasoning: With a,2m,b,m,c equally spaced by d, Wb=3Gm²/d, Wa=(2+1/3)Gm²/d and Wc=(1+2/3)Gm²/d. These explicit pair contributions verify b>a>c; all works are positive because U∞=0 and final U<0.
assumptions: The approaching particle has mass m; the two source particles stay fixed; initial distance is infinite.
